Part 1: Developing Data Pipelines

1.1 Objective

The pipeline processes the H resale flat datasets covering January 2012 to December 2016.

It is designed to:

  • ingest and combine the required H resale source files;
  • preserve the contributing source files in the Raw output;
  • validate and standardise the data;
  • recalculate the remaining lease;
  • remove duplicate transactions;
  • flag potentially unusual resale prices;
  • create the Resale Identifier;
  • generate an irreversible SHA-256 hash of the identifier;
  • produce Raw, Cleaned, Failed, Review, Transformed and Hashed datasets.

1.2 Processing flow

Preserve raw source files
Combine and filter records
Profile data quality
→

2. Clean and Validate

Validate and standardise
Recalculate remaining lease
Remove duplicate transactions
Flag unusual prices
Failed
Invalid or lower-priced duplicates
Review
Valid records with unusual prices
→

3. Create Outputs

Cleaned dataset
Create Resale Identifier
Transformed dataset
Apply SHA-256
Hashed dataset

The Review dataset is a non-exclusive subset of the Cleaned dataset. Records with unusual resale prices are retained in the Cleaned dataset because a statistical anomaly is not necessarily an invalid transaction.

1.4 Data Processing Rules

1.4.1 Ingestion and Profiling

The pipeline reads the original ZIP file programmatically, discovers the source CSV files and filters records from January 2012 to December 2016.

Source schemas are combined into a single master dataset. Missing columns in older source files are added with null values to preserve a consistent schema.

The original contributing CSV files are retained in the Raw output.

Data profiling outputs include:

  • null counts and percentages;
  • column data types;
  • distinct-value counts;
  • categorical distributions for town, flat type, flat model and storey range.

1.4.2 Validation and Cleaning

Validation rules are applied to:

month
town
flat_type
flat_model
storey_range
block
street_name
floor_area_sqm
lease_commence_date
resale_price

The rules cover date formats, required values, valid category domains, storey-range structure and reasonable numeric values.

1.4.3 Remaining Lease

The remaining lease is recalculated using:

  • a 99-year lease duration;
  • the lease commencement year;
  • a configurable as_of_date. (it is used to make the output reproducible)

The result is rounded down and expressed in years and months.

1.4.4 Duplicate Handling

The composite key consists of all original business columns except resale_price.

When duplicate keys have different prices:

  • the higher-priced record is retained;
  • The lower-priced record is written to the Failed dataset with the failure reason DUPLICATE_LOWER_PRICE.

1.4.5 Price Anomaly Detection

Potential resale-price anomalies are identified using price per square metre:

price_per_sqm = resale_price / floor_area_sqm

Records are grouped by resale year, town and flat type. The interquartile range method is then applied:

Lower Bound = Q1 - 1.5 × IQR
Upper Bound = Q3 + 1.5 × IQR

Flagged records remain in the Cleaned dataset and are also written to the Review dataset because a statistical anomaly is not necessarily invalid data.

1.4.6 Resale Identifier and Hashing

The Resale Identifier follows the required structure:

S + BBB + AA + MM + T

Where:

  • BBB is derived from the numeric part of the block;
  • AA is derived from the grouped average resale price;
  • MM is the resale month;
  • T is the first character of the town.

The identifier is hashed using SHA-256 with UTF-8 encoding, and the Hashed output contains only the hash value.

Since the identifier uses grouped and shortened attributes, different transactions may share the same identifier.

Part 2: Architecting Data Ingestion & Data Exploitation Solution Patterns

AWS Data Ingestion & Data Exploitation Architecture

2.1 AWS Data Ingestion Architecture

2.1.1 Objective

The solution ingests batch files from the public data.gov.sg endpoint into S3.

The design supports:

  • files larger than 100 MB;
  • processing within private subnets;
  • controlled outbound internet access;
  • secure storage in S3;
  • automated ETL processing and monitoring.

2.1.2 Processing Flow

The workflow is:

  1. EventBridge Scheduler starts the Step Functions workflow.
  2. Step Functions runs the downloader(python application packaged as a Docker container) on ECS Fargate.
  3. The downloader accesses data.gov.sg through the NAT Gateway and Internet Gateway.
  4. The file is uploaded to the S3 Raw Zone through the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint using multipart upload.
  5. After the download and S3 upload succeed, Step Functions starts the AWS Glue ETL job.
  6. AWS Glue implements the Part 1 ETL logic.
  7. The processed datasets are written to the S3 Processed Zone and registered in the Glue Data Catalog.
  8. CloudWatch collects logs and metrics, while SNS sends failure notifications.

It accesses data.gov.sg through:

2.2 AWS Data Exploitation Architecture

2.2.1 Objective

The solution allows internal users to analyse the processed H resale datasets through Tableau and Athena.

The design supports:

  • private access to Tableau;
  • serverless SQL queries with Athena;
  • metadata management through the AWS Glue Data Catalog;
  • partitioned Parquet data in S3;
  • controlled query results, encryption and monitoring.

2.2.2 Processing Flow

The workflow is:

  1. Internal users access Tableau through a private connection or VPN.
  2. Tableau runs on EC2 in a private subnet without a public IP address.
  3. Tableau submits SQL queries to Athena through the Athena JDBC driver.
  4. The Athena Interface VPC Endpoint provides private access to the Athena API.
  5. Athena reads table and partition metadata from the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
  6. Athena queries the partitioned Parquet datasets in the S3 Processed Zone.
  7. Query results are written to the S3 Athena Query Results bucket.
  8. The Athena Workgroup controls the result location, encryption and query limits.
  9. IAM provides access control, while CloudWatch provides logging, metrics and monitoring.

Tableau runs on EC2 in a Private analytics subnet within the Analytics VPC and has no public IP address.

Internal users access Tableau through an approved private connection or VPN:

Internal Users
→ Corporate Network / VPN
→ Tableau on EC2

2.3 Design Assumptions and Considerations

2.3.1 General Assumptions

  • The ingestion and analytics workloads are deployed in separate VPCs for isolation.
  • Both VPCs use private subnets across at least two Availability Zones.
  • AWS Glue implements the same business rules as the Part 1 Python ETL pipeline.

2.3.2 Security

  • ECS Fargate and Tableau have no public IP addresses.
  • IAM roles follow the principle of least privilege.
  • S3 uses blocked public access and SSE-KMS encryption.
  • Athena and S3 are accessed through VPC endpoints where applicable.

2.3.3 Scalability and Reliability

  • ECS Fargate and AWS Glue can scale as required.
  • S3 multipart upload supports large files and retries of failed parts.
  • Step Functions starts AWS Glue only after the Fargate task succeeds.

2.3.4 Performance

  • Processed datasets are stored in Parquet format and partitioned by resale year and month.
  • Athena scans only the relevant partitions, improving query performance and reducing cost.

2. Overview & Quick Review

TOC30-second summaryWhat the interviewer should remember2-minute project overviewQuick ReviewTen facts to rememberLast-minute Interview Q&A

30-second summary

I built a modular Python ETL pipeline for H resale data from January 2012 to December 2016. It performs schema union, profiling, validation, lease recalculation, duplicate resolution, anomaly detection, identifier creation, and SHA-256 hashing.

I then designed an AWS architecture that operationalises the pipeline using EventBridge, Step Functions, ECS Fargate, S3, AWS Glue, Athena, Tableau, VPC endpoints, monitoring, and encryption.

What the interviewer should remember

  • Programmatic and reproducible
  • Clear output reconciliation
  • Private traffic where possible
  • Simple, scalable, and maintainable

2-minute project overview

The solution has two parts. Part 1 is a Python ETL pipeline. It reads the source files directly, combines different schemas, profiles the master dataset, validates important fields, recalculates the remaining lease, resolves duplicate transactions, and flags unusual prices for review.

After cleaning, the pipeline creates the required Resale Identifier, produces a transformed dataset, and applies SHA-256 to create the hashed output. It produces Raw, Cleaned, Failed, Review, Transformed, and Hashed outputs.

Part 2 operationalises the pipeline on AWS. A scheduled workflow runs a containerised downloader on ECS Fargate inside a private application subnet. Public data is downloaded through a NAT Gateway, while uploads to S3 use a private S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint. AWS Glue then implements the Part 1 logic at scale.

For analytics, Tableau runs on EC2 in a private analytics subnet and uses the Athena JDBC Driver. The Athena API call is kept private through an Athena Interface VPC Endpoint. Athena reads metadata from the Glue Data Catalog, scans partitioned Parquet data in S3, and writes query results to a separate S3 location.

Quick Review

Last-minute Interview Q&A

Q: Why is Review not Failed?

A: Review contains statistically unusual records that remain valid. Failed contains records that violate validation or duplicate-resolution rules.

Q: What is the exact Resale Identifier format?

A: The format is S plus BBB plus AA plus MM plus T. BBB comes from the block, AA from grouped average price, MM from the month, and T from the first letter of the town.

Q: What is the difference between a NAT Gateway and an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint?

A: A NAT Gateway provides controlled outbound internet access from a private subnet. An S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint provides a private route to S3 without using the public internet or NAT.

Q: What do the Athena Interface Endpoint and Private DNS do?

A: The interface endpoint keeps Athena API calls inside the AWS network. Private DNS resolves the normal Athena service hostname to the private endpoint addresses inside the VPC.

Q: Why does Athena not use the customer VPC endpoint when scanning S3?

A: Athena is a managed AWS service. Its service-side workers access S3 through the AWS service network. The customer endpoint is used by resources inside the customer VPC, such as Tableau on EC2, not by Athena workers.

Q: What is the trade-off between one VPC and two VPCs?

A: One VPC is simpler and cheaper to operate. Two VPCs provide stronger workload isolation and separate network controls, but require more routing, endpoint, security, and operational management.

3. Data Quality

Profiling before validation

I first profile the combined master dataset to understand row counts, data types, missing values, distinct values, numeric distributions, and categorical domains.

This allows validation rules to be based on the statistical properties of the master dataset, instead of relying only on hard-coded assumptions.

Core validation rules

Field
Validation approach
Date
Parseable year-month and restricted to January 2012 through December 2016.
Town
Non-null and within the observed canonical town domain.
Flat Type
Non-null and within the observed canonical flat-type domain.
Flat Model
Non-null and normalised against the observed model domain.
storey_range
Must match the expected range pattern and observed domain.

Remaining lease

I assume a 99-year lease. The lease expiry date is derived from the lease commencement year, and the remaining duration is calculated against the configured as-of date.

The output is rounded down into complete years and remaining months. A fixed as-of date makes test results reproducible; in production it would normally be the execution date.

Duplicate handling

The composite key contains every column except resale price. Within each duplicate-key group, records are sorted by resale price in descending order.

The highest-priced record is retained. Lower-priced records are moved to the Failed dataset with an explicit failure reason.

Exact duplicates are also resolved deterministically so that each business event appears only once.

Price anomaly heuristic

Potential anomalies are detected using a robust Median Absolute Deviation approach within suitable peer groups.

A robust method is preferable to a simple mean and standard deviation because resale-price distributions can be skewed and contain legitimate extremes.

Anomalies are flagged for Review rather than automatically rejected. Therefore, the Review dataset is a non-exclusive subset of Cleaned and is not counted as a separate reconciliation category.

4. Identifier & Hash

Resale Identifier format

SBBBPPMMT
S Fixed prefix
BBB First three block digits, left-padded with zeroes
PP First two digits of grouped average resale price
MM Transaction month
T First character of town

Construction example

For block 19, the block component becomes 019. If the grouped average resale price starts with 23, the price component is 23. For January in Ang Mo Kio, the final components are 01 and A.

The resulting identifier follows the required structure: S0192301A.

Hashing decision

I use SHA-256 because it is deterministic, irreversible for practical use, widely supported, and has an extremely low collision probability.

Hashing preserves the practical one-to-one mapping of distinct identifier values, but it does not make duplicate source identifiers unique. Therefore, duplicate handling must happen before hashing.

How I explain the network

The downloader has no public IP address. To reach the public data.gov.sg endpoint, outbound traffic follows: private application subnet → NAT Gateway → Internet Gateway → data.gov.sg.

The upload path is different. S3 traffic follows: private application subnet → S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint → S3, so it does not need to traverse the public Internet.

The NAT Gateway is placed in a public subnet because it needs a route to the Internet Gateway. The Fargate task remains in the private application subnet.

Large-file support

The downloader streams or temporarily stores the source file and uploads it with the AWS SDK. S3 multipart upload splits a large object into parts, retries failed parts independently, and completes them as one object.

Step Functions starts AWS Glue only after the downloader and S3 upload complete successfully.

Security and operations

Control
Purpose
Private subnet
No public IP for the downloader.
NAT Gateway
Controlled outbound access to the public source.
S3 Gateway Endpoint
Private S3 access from the VPC.
SSE-KMS and versioning
Protect and preserve Raw data.
CloudWatch
Logs, metrics, and alarms.
SNS
Failure notifications.
Least-privilege IAM
Restricts service access.

Why ECS Fargate instead of Lambda

The requirement includes files larger than 100 MB. Fargate gives more control over memory, ephemeral storage, execution duration, dependencies, and streaming behaviour.

Lambda could work for some files, but Fargate is a safer general-purpose choice for a containerised large-file downloader.

Why Step Functions

Step Functions makes sequencing explicit: run the downloader, wait for success, then start Glue. It also provides retries, failure handling, execution history, and operational visibility.

Why Glue instead of running pandas in production

The Part 1 implementation demonstrates the business logic in Python and pandas. Glue can reimplement the same logic using PySpark or equivalent distributed processing when data volume grows.

The architecture does not assume that the exact local pandas process is copied unchanged into Glue.

Architecture

→

Private traffic flow

Tableau is hosted on EC2 in a private analytics subnet and has no public IP address. Internal users reach it through an approved corporate network connection or VPN.

The Athena JDBC Driver submits queries through the Athena Interface VPC Endpoint. With Private DNS enabled, the standard Athena service hostname resolves to private endpoint IP addresses inside the VPC.

Athena itself is a managed AWS service. It reads table and partition metadata from the Glue Data Catalog, scans processed Parquet data in S3, and writes results to a separate S3 query-results location.

Where the driver retrieves result files directly from S3, EC2 uses the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint to keep that S3 traffic private.

Why two types of private subnet names

Private Application Subnet hosts the ingestion workload, such as ECS Fargate.

Private Analytics Subnet hosts the consumption workload, such as Tableau on EC2.

They represent different workload boundaries. They may be in separate VPCs for stronger isolation, although a shared VPC with separate subnets could also work in a smaller environment.

One VPC or two VPCs?

Two VPCs provide clearer separation between ingestion and analytics workloads, independent routing and endpoint policies, and a smaller blast radius.

A single VPC with separate application and analytics subnets would be simpler and cheaper. For this design, two logical VPCs make the security boundaries easier to explain, but the choice is an architectural assumption rather than a hard requirement.

One subnet or multiple subnets?

A single subnet is enough to explain the basic requirement. Multiple subnets across Availability Zones improve availability and provide more scheduling choices.

However, two subnets alone do not make Tableau highly available. True Tableau high availability would also require multiple application instances and appropriate load balancing or clustering.

9. Interview Story

Recommended presentation order

  1. Start with the business objective: clean and transform resale data for analysis.
  2. Explain Part 1 as a controlled data lifecycle: Raw → Cleaned/Failed/Review → Transformed → Hashed.
  3. Highlight three difficult rules: schema union, duplicate resolution, and Resale Identifier construction.
  4. Explain operationalisation: schedule → Fargate → S3 Raw → Glue → S3 Processed.
  5. Finish with exploitation: Tableau → private Athena API → Catalog/S3 → query results.
  6. State the trade-offs: simple design first, with clear paths to scale and improve availability.

Opening answer

I approached the assignment as both a data-engineering problem and an operational architecture problem. First, I built a reproducible Python pipeline with explicit data-quality controls and traceable outputs. Then I designed an AWS solution that preserves the same logic while separating ingestion, processing, storage, and analytics concerns.

Closing answer

The main strength of my solution is that every record has a clear outcome, every major processing rule is testable, and every network path has an explicit security purpose. The design is intentionally simple enough to operate, while still allowing the downloader, Glue processing, storage layout, and analytics layer to scale independently.

8. Interview Q&A

High-probability interview questions

Question
Strong answer
Why did you keep anomalous prices in Cleaned?
The task asks me to identify anomalies, not automatically reject them. A high or low price may still be a legitimate transaction, so I flag it for review.
How do you prove output completeness?
I reconcile source rows against retained and rejected records. Review is a subset of Cleaned, so it is excluded from additive reconciliation.
Why use a composite key excluding resale price?
That rule comes directly from the assignment. It models two records as the same transaction when every non-price attribute matches.
What happens when two records have the same key and same price?
I keep one deterministically and classify the additional exact copy as a duplicate.
Why SHA-256?
It is deterministic, practically irreversible, widely supported, and has negligible collision risk for this use case.
Does SHA-256 guarantee source uniqueness?
No. It preserves distinctions between different inputs in practical use, but duplicate input identifiers still produce duplicate hashes.
Why use a NAT Gateway?
The private downloader needs controlled outbound access to a public endpoint while remaining without a public IP.
Why use an S3 Gateway Endpoint?
It keeps VPC-to-S3 traffic on the AWS network and avoids sending S3 traffic through the NAT Gateway.
Why use an Athena Interface Endpoint?
The Tableau Athena Driver normally calls the Athena service endpoint. PrivateLink and Private DNS keep that API traffic private.
Does Athena scan S3 through my VPC endpoint?
No. Athena is a managed service and accesses S3 on the service side. The S3 endpoint is for resources inside my VPC, such as Tableau EC2.

What this role is really about

This role combines Senior Data Engineering, Cloud Architecture, Data & AI Platform Engineering, and Technical Leadership.

The core outcome is a secure, scalable, governed platform that converts business requirements into reliable data products and AI-ready services.

LakehouseETL / ELTCloud ArchitectureDataOpsMLOps / LLMOpsGovernanceLeadership

60-second role summary

The position is responsible for designing scalable cloud data architectures, leading Lakehouse development, and building reliable production-grade ETL and ELT pipelines. It also covers cloud migration, Infrastructure as Code, platform security, governance, DataOps, MLOps or LLMOps, technical documentation, stakeholder communication, and mentoring.

1. Data Pipeline Infrastructure & Architecture

Design the platform before building individual jobs.

🏗️
Scalable architecture

Separate ingestion, storage, processing, serving, governance, and monitoring so that each layer can scale independently.

🏔️
Data Lakehouse

Combines low-cost object storage with warehouse-style ACID transactions, schema management, and analytical performance.

🛡️
High availability and security

Use multi-zone design, retries, encryption, least-privilege access, private networking, backup, and recovery controls.

2. Pipeline Development & Optimisation

Build pipelines that are correct, observable, efficient, and recoverable.

🔄
ETL vs ELT

ETL transforms before loading into the target; ELT loads first and transforms using the target platform's compute engine.

⚡
Optimisation

Improve partitioning, file size, joins, shuffle, caching, incremental loading, and resource configuration.

✅
Data quality and monitoring

Validate freshness, completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, and reconciliation; alert on SLA or rule failures.

3. Data Systems Architecting & Solutioning

Translate business goals into an executable technical design.

🧭
Requirement translation

Convert business outcomes into data sources, SLAs, scale, security, integration, availability, and cost requirements.

☁️
Cloud migration

Assess the current platform, define a target architecture, migrate in phases, validate data, and control cutover risk.

📐
Architecture documentation

Maintain diagrams, decisions, interfaces, data flows, security controls, operational procedures, and trade-offs.

4. Cloud Platform Operations

Operate the data platform as a governed product, not a collection of scripts.

🧱
Terraform and Infrastructure as Code

Define repeatable cloud infrastructure in version-controlled code instead of configuring resources manually.

🔐
IAM

Identity and Access Management controls who can access which resource and which actions they can perform.

🌐
Network architecture

Use VPCs, public and private subnets, routing, security groups, NAT, and private endpoints to control traffic paths.

5. DataOps, MLOps & LLMOps

Apply software-engineering discipline to data and AI lifecycles.

🔧
DataOps

CI/CD, testing, orchestration, observability, lineage, incident response, and reliable data delivery.

🤖
MLOps

Manage feature pipelines, experiments, model registry, deployment, monitoring, retraining, and governance.

🧠
LLMOps

Manage prompts, RAG, agents, evaluation, guardrails, model versions, latency, token cost, and observability.

6. Technical Leadership & Collaboration

Lead through architecture, standards, communication, and mentoring.

🗣️
Stakeholder communication

Explain the problem, options, trade-offs, recommendation, risk, and expected business outcome.

🔍
Architecture review

Challenge assumptions and review scalability, reliability, security, cost, operability, and maintainability.

🌱
Mentoring

Help junior engineers improve design, debugging, testing, documentation, and independent decision-making.
